tier1.text: The epididymis is a coiled tube where sperm mature and are stored until ejaculation. As sperm pass through the epididymis, they gain the power to move on their own. The epididymis lies along the top and back of the testis, the organ that makes sperm. Straightened out, the tightly coiled epididymis would be about 6 meters (20 feet) long.

tier2.text: The epididymis carries, stores and matures sperm on their way from the testis, the male organ that produces sperm. Each epididymis is a comma-shaped organ along the top and back edges of a testis. The head of the epididymis receives several efferent ductules, the ducts through which sperm leave the testis. The head then drains into a single, wider duct that forms the body and tail of the epididymis. Tightly coiled, the epididymis takes up little room, but straightened out, the whole tube would be about 6 meters (20 feet) long. Smooth muscle, a muscle under involuntary control that moves internal organs, lines the tubes of the epididymis and pushes sperm along by contracting. On average, sperm take 12 days to pass through the coils of the epididymis. As sperm travel the length of the epididymis, they mature further and gain the ability to move under their own power. The more mature sperm are then stored in the tail, the final section of the epididymis, until ejaculation. During ejaculation, smooth muscle contractions push sperm out of the tail into the ductus deferens (vas deferens), the duct that carries sperm away from the epididymis.
